song.title: Get Up (I Feel Like Being A) Sex Machine

guitar.evidence: Jimmy Nolen, James Brown's guitarist who pioneered the 'chicken scratch' funk rhythm style, is documented as a Fender Telecaster/Mustang player; well known among funk historians though James Brown himself wasn't the guitarist.

tone.target: dry funk rhythm with percussive scratch and slight breakup
tone.profile: dry funk rhythm with percussive scratch and slight breakup
tone.summary: A punchy, dry signal chain utilizing Compression for attack definition, followed by the US Deluxe/Silver Twin tone into a 2x12 cabinet to achieve the required 'chank' and snap.
corrections: keep it cleaner than light crunch

rig.name: James Brown - Get Up (I Feel Like Being A) Sex Machine - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up any unwanted hum or noise from the percussive playing style.
Enhance the attack and sustain slightly for a punchy, defined 'chank' rhythm.
Keep the tone clean and focused on percussive rhythm rather than heavy crunch.
Simulate the clean, bright Fender-style tone required for funk rhythm.
Provide a bright, focused sound suitable for tight funk rhythm and single-coil tones.
Tuck the mids slightly and boost high end to maximize 'snap' and definition in the mix.
Avoid wah as per the musical verdict and keep the tone direct.
Avoid chorus and vibrato as specified in the corrections.
Avoid big delay to maintain the dry funk feel.
Add a subtle sense of space ('small room') without washing out the tight rhythm.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for better definition in funk rhythm.

proposals.reason: Enhance the punch and clarity needed for tight funk chank.
